summary: Most owners report a tough, simple blender that turns out very smooth blends and often lasts a decade or more, with replacement parts easy to find. It is loud, and a few newer units felt lighter and cheaper. The tall container suits smoothies but small batches and thick blends need the tamper.

Most owners use it as a main oven and toaster oven, praising ease of use, solid build and even cooking. Cleaning is the biggest complaint, especially after greasy air frying, and many say it air fries worse than a dedicated basket fryer. Some units fail within a few years, often the fan, screen or door.

Most owners find it a durable mixer, with many reporting ten years or more of regular use for cakes, cookies and light bread. It struggles with stiff or large doughs, where it gets loud, bounces and can overheat or strip gears. Best for cakes and cookies, less so for frequent bread.

Most owners report a durable, no-fuss pressure cooker, with many still using one after eight to ten years for beans, rice, soups and stews. Complaints are scattered: sealing rings holding smells, weak sauté and slow cook, burn warnings, and some units failing to seal or dying. Well suited to simple, everyday cooking.

Most owners find it a powerful blender that makes very smooth smoothies, with easy presets and a solid feel. Downsides include container detection problems with attachments and some units developing errors, burning smells or turning on by themselves. The wide containers also suit single servings poorly.

Many owners like having a pressure cooker and an air fryer lid in one pot, finding it easy to use and good for crisping for one or two people. The air fryer is small and awkward, and more demanding to clean than a standalone. Some lids throw errors such as LID or burn notices.

Most owners who upgraded like the handled inner pot, the better sauté and the extra settings, and find it easy to use. Reliability is the main concern, with a good number of reports of units stuck in preheat, not reaching pressure or failing after a year or two. Slow cook and sous vide get mixed reports.

Reviews are split: many find it handy for single smoothies, sauces, dressings and grinding, easy to use and clean. A large share report the motor or base giving out within months to a couple of years, and it struggles with ice and frozen fruit. Some units last many years, so durability is a gamble.

Most owners praise it as a powerful, well built blender with handy presets that makes very smooth results and often runs for ten years. It is loud, and the wide low container needs larger batches. Some units failed, mostly start switches and motors, and a few had rust or discoloration on the housing.

Most owners like it for being easy to clean, easy to use, quick and fairly quiet. Food cooks fast and hot, so standard times often need trimming. A few report a plastic smell, hot spots or units that stopped working early, but those are in the minority.

Most owners see it as good value, with strong enough power for smooth smoothies and a narrow container that suits small batches. It is loud, some units went wrong, and a few struggled with thick blends or compared it unfavorably to a Ninja. Best for smoothies for one or two.

Reviewers who like it praise its air frying, sous vide and secure-feeling lid. A large majority of the complaints are about reliability, with the lid sticking shut after cooking, failing to build pressure or throwing remove-cover errors, and some air fryer elements stopping. Several explicitly advise against this version.

Most owners like it as a good-value Vitamix with simple controls, a timer and app presets, making very smooth smoothies. The main downside is the self-detect containers and cups, which sometimes go unrecognized or fail, and a few units overheated or broke. Wide jars also suit small batches poorly.

Reviews are split. Several owners love it for pressure cooking, the quiet steam release and years of reliable use. A large share report problems such as failing to reach pressure, stuck preheat, lid errors, burn notices and units dying. Slow cook and sauté also draw mixed comments.

Most owners find the bowl-lift sturdy and stronger than a tilt-head, handling bread, cookie dough and pasta with little bouncing. A noticeable group report new units dying after a few uses or stopping mid-mix. Small dough batches can be left unmixed at the bottom of the wide bowl.

Most owners like the presets and find it easy to use, with smooth results and a solid feel. It is loud, and a good number of reviewers report blends that stall, air pockets or smoothies needing extra liquid, especially in small batches. A few units had errors or motor faults.

Most owners like it as a simple, powerful Vitamix with a long warranty and good smoothies, often bought as a Costco bundle. The most common complaint is noise, and the personal cup adapter is fiddly for some. The wide low container needs larger batches, and a few units broke or leaked.

Most owners call it a powerful, durable blender, quieter than many Vitamix models, with several still using one after ten years or more. Failures do show up, such as the start switch, speed dial or motor, and the wide low container is poor for small batches. Thick blends can stall without the tamper.

Owners like how easy it is to use, how it crisps and cooks fast, and its rotisserie and multiple trays. Reliability is the main concern, with many reporting the display fading or failing and other faults after the warranty. A plastic smell at first, noise and awkward cleaning also come up repeatedly.

Most owners praise the two heating elements, which cook evenly without much shaking or preheating, and many find it easy to use and fast. A smaller group report the nonstick coating wearing, screens failing after months, or a plastic smell. The basket is wide rather than deep.

Most owners love the Ninja Crispi Pro AS101 for how easy it is to clean, since the glass containers go in the dishwasher and the food can be watched while it cooks. Several use it daily and it has replaced the oven or an older air fryer for many. A few report undercooked food, loud beeps or failures.

Most owners find the Instant Vortex 6-Qt simple to use and reliable, with several using it daily for years. The main downside is a burnt plastic smell. For some it fades after a couple of uses or burn-offs, but a number of owners could never get rid of it and returned the unit.

Owners who like the Instant Pot Rio Wide praise its wide, shallow pot, which makes sautéing, browning and stirring easier, and some find it quiet. The main concern is reliability: several report buttons, the lid sensor, the float valve or power failing within months, and replacement parts such as sealing rings are hard to find. It also takes up a lot of counter space.

Some owners find the Kenwood kMix well built and quiet for everyday baking, and a few have used it for years. The main downside is reliability: many report the glass bowl's plastic locking ring seizing so the bowl will not release, along with motor, gear and head-release failures. Repairs were often needed.

Most owners love the Vitamix Propel 750, mentioning smooth results, a fairly quiet motor and a size that fits under the counter, and several use it for single servings. A few report early failures such as overheating, cracking or a unit that stopped working, and a couple found it weaker than a Ninja for small smoothies.

Some owners like the Philips Essential Airfryer XL HD9270 for being easy to use and quiet. The main downside is durability: many report it stopping heating when a small plastic part that triggers the basket-closed sensor breaks, plus rust on the base and a basket coating that wears off. A few find the basket small or food not crispy.

Most owners like the Ninja Foodi Dual Zone AF300 for being easy to use and for the sync function that finishes two drawers together, and it does chicken, fish and chips well. The main complaint is uneven results with some foods, such as fries coming out burnt or undercooked and baking being poor. A couple find it small.

Most owners use the Breville Smart Oven Air Fryer BOV860 daily as a versatile oven that bakes, toasts and air fries, often in place of a full oven. Air frying is good but the fan can be loud and the drip tray is hard to clean once burnt on. A few report it getting stuck on preheat in air-fry mode.

Most owners like the Instant Vortex Plus 6-Qt ClearCook for crispy results and the window that lets food be watched while it cooks. The main downside is the internal light, which several report burning out within months. A few mention a lingering plastic smell, or window residue and cracking that is hard to clean.

Owners are mostly very happy with the Vitamix Ascent X4, using its programs daily for smoothies, soup and nut butter and finding it smooth and quieter than other blenders they have had. A few have complaints such as the tall height, the touch panel, or a top layer that does not blend.

Most owners like the Vitamix Propel 510, describing it as easy to use, powerful and well suited to a 48 oz container, with handy presets. Noise is the main complaint, with several finding it very loud, though one calls it among the quieter Vitamix models. A few report a loose pitcher or splashing from the lid.

A few owners like the Instant Omni Plus for its large capacity and easy cleaning. The main downside is reliability: many report failures such as getting stuck on preheat, a dead fan, screen or button faults, and replacement parts are hard to get. Several also find food cooks unevenly, burnt outside and raw inside.

Owners who like the Ninja Foodi FlexDrawer AF500 find it easy to use, enjoy cooking two things at different settings that finish together, and like the large space when the divider is removed. Downsides are its bulk: the heavy drawer is awkward to wash and the unit slides on the counter when the stiff drawer is opened. A couple had trouble with the stop-one-zone feature.

Some owners are happy with the Ninja Foodi DualZone DZ201 for cooking two things at once. The main complaint is reliability: many report one basket shutting off after a few minutes in Match Cook, sometimes within months. A few find the two baskets heat differently, and some wish for a single large basket.

Owners like that the Ninja Foodi PossibleCooker Pro MC1001 is easy to clean and sears and slow cooks in the same pot. The main complaint is that its slow cook settings do not behave like a regular slow cooker. Some find food cooks too fast, others that low never gets food tender, so times need adjusting. The nonstick pot is also described as fragile.

Most owners rate the Typhur Dome very highly, praising its easy-to-clean ceramic basket, quiet running and even, crispy results. The main downside is its low height, which can leave food too close to the top element. A few mention smoke or disappointing self-clean.

Most owners love the Vitamix Ascent X5 for its smooth blends, sturdy build and programs, and several came from a Ninja or Blendtec. A few were less sure, saying a cheaper model would do since they ignore the presets, or that the included container felt small. One had a self-detect container stop working.

Some owners like the Ninja Foodi Multifunction Oven DT200 and use it in place of a regular oven, and several have had it working for years. The main complaint is failure, with a blower fan that stops spinning and error codes, and repairs or parts are hard to find. A few also say the outer sides get dangerously hot.

Most owners like the Cosori Smart Air Fryer Toaster Oven CS130 as a roomy, easy-to-use oven that handles pizza, roasting and baking and can replace a regular oven. Downsides are mixed and individual: it gets dirty like any oven, exposed elements smoke with grease, and one owner's unit stopped heating after a while.

Most reviewers buy the Ninja Crispi FN101 for how easy it is to clean, with glass bowls that go in the dishwasher and double as storage. It suits one or two people. Air frying is weaker than in standard air fryers for some, with lower power and less crisping, and temperature settings are ranges rather than exact.

Most owners find the Vitamix Ascent A2300 easy to use and blend very smooth, from smoothies to soups and nut butters. The main downside is container and jug detection: a fair number report cups or jugs not being recognised or faults appearing, sometimes needing replacements. Some find it loud, and the large containers awkward for small batches.

Most reviewers find the Vitamix Alta Pro powerful, with smooth results and handy smoothie, soup and self-clean presets. Some report a burning plastic smell, a few got faulty units that were swapped, and it can be loud. The wide low-profile jar is awkward for small batches, which some solve with a smaller container.

Most owners find the KitchenAid 6.6 L Bowl-Lift sturdy and strong, handling heavy bread and large batches while staying put and running quieter than smaller mixers. Quality control is the worry: a number report new units grinding, cutting out or arriving with loose parts, and some find it loud. It is too big for small batches.

Most reviewers praise this bowl-lift for its power and stability with bread dough, stiff cookie batters and double batches, and many older ones keep running for years. Some newer units died or stalled on dough, and a few report clicking or grinding. It is tall and big, so small quantities are better done with a hand mixer.

The smaller Rio Mini gets the most love, with fans praising its wide, low pot for sautéing and its simple controls for one or two people. Reliability complaints are more common, though: many report long preheating, burn warnings, failing to reach pressure, and some units that stopped working. Reviews are split by size.

Most owners use the Breville Smart Oven Pro BOV845 daily in place of the big oven, liking its quick preheat, even heating and sturdy feel. The main downside is durability: many report the convection fan failing or getting loud after a few years, with parts hard to find. Air frying is fine but not as good as a basket air fryer.

Most owners like how fast the Ninja Foodi Digital Air Fry Oven SP101 heats, how simple the controls are and that it flips up against the wall to save counter space. Cleaning is the main complaint, with grease baking onto elements and trays. Some units failed early or cooked unevenly, and air frying is not quite as good as a basket fryer.

Most owners find the Vitamix 5300 a long-lasting workhorse, with many still using one after a decade or more and often bought refurbished. It blends smoothies and fibrous produce very smooth. Downsides are noise, and parts wearing out eventually, such as container bearings and drive sockets. The low-profile container is awkward for thick or small batches.

Fans use the Ninja Combi SFP701 daily for quick full meals, rice, steamed dishes and air frying, and find the steam keeps it cleaner. The main worry is reliability: many report units dying or glitching within months. A few notice a plastic smell or chipping pan coating, and it cannot pressure cook.

When it works, owners like the Instant Pot Pro Plus for its easy operation, auto venting and phone notifications. Reliability is the main complaint: many report heating or preheat errors, steam release trouble or units failing after a year or two, with support hard to get. The Wi-Fi app is limited to status in some experiences.

Many owners have kept a Classic tilt-head running for decades and call it a dependable workhorse for baking. Age shows in some: failing motors or speed controls, noise, and flaking beater coating. A few new units died on dough, and the small bowl limits big batches. It handles light to moderate dough better than heavy bread.

Most owners love the Ninja Flip Toaster Oven SP151 for flipping up out of the way, heating fast and handling toasting, air frying and pizza in one. Cleaning around the elements is the main complaint. A few had units fail, burn the bottoms of food, or find it loud, and some prefer drawer air fryers.

Most owners find the Ninja Air Fryer AF101 simple, sturdy and good value, using it for years for everyday foods. It is compact, enough for one or two people. Downsides are the small basket, grease building up around the heating element that is hard to clean, and light foods blowing around. A few units failed.

Most owners find the Instant Pot Pro Crisp easy to use, pressure cooking as well as other pots, with the air fryer lid handy for one or two people and for crisping skin on whole chickens. The air fryer side is limited by small capacity and uneven heat, and it is big and heavy. A few had units fail.

Most owners praise the Typhur Dome 2 for even, crispy results across its wide tray and easy cleaning. It cooks lots of food without flipping. Downsides are its large footprint and shallow height for tall items, and a couple report smoke with fatty meats. Some say it needs hotter settings when full.

Most owners like the Vitamix Ascent X2 for its physical knob and switches, useful smoothie and self-clean presets, and smooth blends, often through a bundle with a food processor. It can be loud, and a few dislike the container detection. A small number report it stopping mid-blend or leaking.

The main complaint on the Ninja Foodi XL Pro Air Fry Oven DT201 is cleaning: many find trays, fan area and elements near impossible to clean. Several say air frying is worse than a basket fryer and heating runs uneven or low, and a number of units died within a year or two. It bakes and toasts well for some.

Reliability is the story with the KitchenAid K400 Blender: most reviewers report the jar leaking from the base, a failing bearing, grease or rusty residue, and a growing noise, often within a year or two. Replacements sometimes failed the same way, and spare jars are costly or hard to find. It is powerful while it works.

Owners who like the Ninja Foodi MAX Dual Zone AF400 say it cooks evenly, runs two batches or one large dish, and suits a family. The main downside is crisper plate coating peeling, reported by several. Some units also threw drawer or startup errors, and the fan can be loud.
